name: Music lessons
what_example: piano lessons for kids and adults

crowd.buyer: Parents, and adults who want to learn

off_season.play: Offer a summer block of 6 lessons and book fall times before school starts.

not_yet: Don't rent a studio before your weekly schedule is full.
Don't promise exam results, audition spots or a set pace.
Don't message students under 18 directly. Talk to parents.
crowd.note: Safety rules with minors come first: parents book, and lessons happen where a parent can see or hear.
crowd.basis: Scores, buyer, first $1 and not-yet lines: research/niches/music.json crowd_scores (our judgment). Best months and the summer dip: a judgment call from the school-year terms in that file's studio policy sources.

safety: For students under 18, parents book and pay. You talk with parents, not students.
Lessons happen where a parent can see or hear: at home with a parent there, in your studio with the door open and parents welcome to sit in, or online with a parent in the house.
No direct messages, texts or social follows with students under 18. Links, notes and reminders go to the parent.
Background check rules for private teachers differ by state, and many parents ask for one: get one in your own name and offer to share it. Follow any rule your state, a school or a program has.
Collect contact details from parents only. The FTC's COPPA rule covers collecting personal information online from children under 13.

extra.title: First call script (15 minutes, free)
lines: 1. Thanks for making time. Who are the lessons for, and what made you think about lessons now?
2. Which instrument, and is there one at home yet? Any lessons or school band before?
3. What would they love to play: a song, a style, music for a school group?
4. Here's how I work: a first lesson to see where they are, a plan for 4 weeks, a practice log for home and a short note after every lesson.
5. Safety: for students under 18 you book and pay, lessons happen where you can see or hear, and I only message you.
6. My founding price is {founding}. Want to pick a first lesson time?

offer.name: Private music lessons
offer.basis: From research/niches/music.json (Ensemble Schools, ArtMaster, Preply, Music to Your Home and Lessons.com pages, checked 2026-10-19). Longer lessons cost more: about $35 to $75 for 45 minutes and $40 to $120 for 60 minutes.
includes: A first lesson that finds where the student is and what they want to play
A plan for the first 4 weeks and a printable practice log for home
A short note after every lesson: what we worked on, what to practice, what's next
A studio policy in writing: missed lessons, payment and recitals
steps: A free 15-minute call: the instrument, the student's age and experience, and times that work.
First lesson: setup and posture, a few things to play, and the plan for the next 4 weeks.
Every lesson: warm up, check the practice log, learn one new thing, play a piece, set the week's practice.
After every lesson you get a short note from me.
offer.promise: If I miss a lesson or I'm late, the next one is free. If the first lesson isn't a fit, I refund it.
offer.promise_note: I don't promise exam results, audition spots or a set pace. I promise the work: every lesson as booked, a plan, and a note after each one.

Lessons happen where you can see or hear: at home with you there, in my studio with the door open and you welcome to sit in, or online with you in the house.
I never message students under 18 directly. Links and reminders go to you.
offer.footer: Pay per lesson or for a block of 4 weekly lessons.

stop.label: Asked you to stop
stop.next: Don't send anything else. They're marked lost so they stay off your lists.

yes.label: They're interested
yes.means: They want to hear more or book.
yes.answer: That's great to hear! The easiest first step is a free 15-minute call: I'll ask about the instrument, the student's age and experience, a song they'd love to play and what times work. When suits you this week?

price.label: They asked the price
price.means: They want the price before anything else.
price.answer: Of course. It's {rate}, {length} one to one, with a plan for the first 4 weeks and a short note after every lesson. Want to start with a free 15-minute call to see if it fits?
price.next: Say the price once, then offer the free first call.

later.label: Not right now
later.answer: No problem at all. Would it help if I checked back before the next school term? Either way, my number's here when you're ready.
later.next: Set a reminder for 4 to 6 weeks, or just before the next term.

who.label: Who is this?
who.means: They want to know who you are first.
who.answer: Sorry, I should have said! I'm {me}, and I teach {what} here in {area}. Parents book for kids, lessons happen where a parent can see or hear, and you get a short note after every lesson. Happy to answer any question.
who.next: Answer plainly, then offer the free first call.

covered.label: They have a teacher
covered.answer: Good to hear you have a teacher! If you ever want a second option, say for a summer block or a second instrument, I'm around. Thanks for letting me know.
covered.next: Leave it there. Ask again before summer if it fits.

question.label: They asked a question
question.answer: Good question! The honest answer depends on the student, so the best way to answer it properly is a free 15-minute call. Would one day this week work?
question.next: Answer it in a line if you can, then offer the free first call.

other.label: Not sure what they meant
other.answer: Thanks for getting back to me! Happy to help however I can. Would a free 15-minute call this week be easier to talk it through?
other.next: Keep it short and end with one question.

talk.label: Wants to talk
talk.answer: Happy to! {when_ask} It's a free 15-minute call: I'll ask about the instrument, the student's age and experience, and what times work.

yes.label: They said yes
yes.answer: Thank you, that's great! I'll drop off a few flyers this week. Is there a day that works best, or someone I should ask for?
yes.next: Drop off the flyers within a week and thank them in person.

price.label: They asked the price
price.means: They want to know what families pay.
price.answer: Families pay {rate}, booked and paid by parents, and the first call is free. Happy to drop off a flyer with the details.
price.next: Say the price once, then offer the flyer.

later.label: Not right now
later.answer: No problem at all. Could I check back next term? Thanks for considering it.
later.next: Set a reminder for next term.

who.label: Who is this?
who.means: They want to know who you are first.
who.answer: Sorry, I should have said! I'm {me}, and I teach {what} locally. Parents book, lessons happen where a parent can see or hear, and I follow your rules on posting. Happy to come by and say hello.
who.next: Answer plainly, then offer to stop by.

covered.label: They have someone
covered.means: They already work with teachers or a program.

covered.next: Ask once about a teacher list, then let it go.

question.label: They asked a question
question.answer: Good question! Happy to answer it properly: could I stop by for five minutes, or would a quick call be easier?
question.next: Answer it in a line if you can, then offer to stop by.

other.label: Not sure what they meant
other.answer: Thanks for getting back to me! Happy to work around your rules. What's the best way to share my info with families?
other.next: Keep it short and end with one question.

partner_objections.label: They have rules
partner_objections.match: \b(polic(y|ies)|not allowed|aren't allowed|can't post|cannot post|no (business|commercial|solicit\w*)|approv\w*|bulletin|board rules|guidelines|background check\w*|clearances?)
partner_objections.means: They have rules about posting, promoting or who works with their families.
partner_objections.answer: Thanks for explaining, and of course I'll follow your rules. Is there an approved way in, like a newsletter, a list of local teachers or a background check you need, that I could apply for?
partner_objections.next: Follow their rules exactly and ask about the approved way in.

objections.label: Can you promise a result?
objections.answer: I can't promise an exam result, an audition or a pace, and I'd be careful with anyone who does. What I can promise is the work: a first lesson to see where things are, a plan for the next 4 weeks, a practice log for home and a short note after every lesson, so you can see what we're working on.
objections.next: Never promise a result. Offer the first lesson and the plan instead.

objections.label: Are you background checked?
objections.means: They want to know how lessons with their child work.
objections.answer: Good question, and every parent should ask it. Here's how lessons work: you book and pay, lessons happen where you can see or hear (at home with you there, in my studio with the door open, or online with you in the house), you're welcome to sit in on any lesson, and I only ever message you, never your child. I'll share my background check report before the first lesson.
objections.next: Send this once your background check report is in hand.
objections.check: Have your background check report ready to share before you send this.

sources.says: Background checks are an important tool but have limitations; youth programs add supervision, a no closed door policy and tell caregivers what their children will be doing.
A background check includes national criminal database, county criminal and sex offender registry searches, and needs written permission under the FCRA.

objections.label: What if we miss a lesson?
objections.means: They want to know the missed lesson rule.
objections.answer: Good to ask up front. With 24 hours' notice you can book a makeup lesson, up to 2 a term. A no-show or a late cancel isn't made up, and if I ever cancel, you get a makeup or a credit. It's all in my studio policy, which I'll send before the first lesson.
objections.next: Answer it, then send your studio policy (Lesson plan and practice log makes it).

sources.says: Make-up lessons at no extra charge with 24 hours advance notice, limited to two a semester; no refunds for missed lessons.
Don't offer make-ups for no-shows or late cancellations (less than 24 hours notice).
If the teacher is absent, a substitute or a rescheduled lesson.

objections.label: Is my child old enough?
objections.match: \b(old enough|too young|what age|how old|ages? do you (teach|take)|is (she|he) ready)\b
objections.means: They wonder whether it's the right time to start.
objections.answer: Good question. It depends on the child more than the birthday. Young children often do well with a 30-minute lesson, and a first lesson is the easiest way to see if now is the right time. Want to book one?
objections.next: Offer a first lesson, 30 minutes for a young child.

sources.says: Young children often do well with a 30-minute lesson.

objections.label: Too old to start?
objections.match: \b(too old|as an adult|adult (student|beginner|lessons?)|at my age|teach adults)\b
objections.means: An adult wonders whether lessons are for them.
objections.answer: Not at all. I teach adults too, and lessons go at your pace, starting with music you want to play. Older and adult students often like a longer lesson, 45 or 60 minutes. Want to try a first lesson?
objections.next: Offer a first lesson and ask what they'd love to play.

sources.says: More experienced students, older students and adult students often benefit from longer lessons.

objections.label: No instrument yet
objections.means: They aren't sure what instrument to get.
objections.answer: No problem at all. Before you buy or rent anything, let's do a first lesson. I'll tell you what to look for and what size fits.
objections.next: Book the first lesson; help them choose after it.

objections.label: Online or in person?
objections.answer: Either works. Online saves the drive; in person can be at your home with you there, or at my studio. Online lessons usually cost about the same as studio lessons, and lessons at your home may have a small travel fee. Which would suit you best?
objections.next: Let them pick, then book the free first call.

sources.says: Online and in-studio lessons cost about the same; in-home lessons cost 10 to 20 percent more.
Are online lessons cheaper? In most cases, no.

objections.label: More than they expected
objections.means: The price feels high to them.
objections.answer: That's fair to ask. Private lessons usually run about $25 to $70 for 30 minutes, depending on the teacher, the area and whether it's online. For {rate} you get one-to-one lessons, a 4-week plan with a practice log, and a note after each lesson. If weekly is a stretch, every other week works too, or a block of 4 paid up front costs a little less per lesson.
objections.next: Hold your price. Offer every other week or the block of 4.

sources.says: 30-minute lessons cost $35 to $50.
In-person piano lessons $40 to $70 for 30 minutes; online $25 to $55.

objections.label: Too busy this season
objections.answer: Totally understand. Two options that fit around a busy season: a 30-minute lesson every other week, or a summer block when things calm down. Would either work?
objections.next: Offer the smaller step, or a reminder before summer.

lesson_plan.length_note: Auto length: 30 minutes for anyone new and for students under 13 with the basics; 45 minutes for students 13 and up with the basics and for intermediate students under 13; 60 minutes for intermediate students 13 and up. Young children often do well with a 30-minute lesson; older, more experienced and adult students often benefit from longer ones (Ensemble Schools, ArtMaster).
lesson_plan.judgment_note: The weekly plans, the lesson parts and the practice minutes are a starting point from teaching judgment, not sourced facts. Change anything that doesn't fit the student.
lesson_plan.adult_line: Practice when it fits your day: short, regular sessions.

policy.title: Studio policy
policy.lessons: Private lessons, one to one, once a week at a set time. Lessons start and end on time, so please be ready to play.

pay.Monthly, in advance: Tuition is paid each month in advance, by the 1st: the price per lesson times the lessons on the calendar that month. Paying holds your weekly time.
pay.Per lesson: Lessons are paid at or before each lesson.
pay.By term, in advance: Tuition is paid by term, in advance, before the first lesson of the term. Paying holds your weekly time.

late.Monthly, in advance: Tuition paid after the 1st has a late fee of {late_fee}.
late.Per lesson: Payment after the lesson has a late fee of {late_fee}.
late.By term, in advance: Tuition paid after the first lesson of the term has a late fee of {late_fee}.

policy.makeups: With that notice you can book a makeup lesson, up to {makeups} a term, used within the same term.
policy.late_cancel: A no-show, or a cancel with less notice, isn't made up or refunded.
policy.sick: If the student is sick, please cancel as early as you can rather than have the lesson.
policy.teacher: If I cancel, you get a makeup lesson or a credit, your choice.
policy.stop: To stop lessons, please tell me {stop} ahead.
policy.recital_usual: Recitals happen once or twice a year.
policy.recital_choice: Taking part is up to each student and family.
policy.recital_fee: Recital fee: {fee} per student, to cover the venue, programs and other costs.
policy.recital_music: Each performer plays from purchased music, not a photocopy.
policy.recital_guests: Families and guests are welcome. Please film only your own child, and never post another child without their parent's yes.
safety: You book and pay, and I talk with you about times and changes.
Lessons happen where you can see or hear: at home with you there, in my studio with the door open, or online with you in the house. You're welcome to sit in on any lesson.
I never message, text or follow students under 18. Notes and links come to you.
I never share a student's photo, video or name without your written yes.
policy.background: Ask me for my background check report any time.
photos_adult: I never share your photo, video or name without your written yes.
Lesson notes, reminders and changes come to you by text or email.

notes.recital_range: Recital fees typically run $20 to $60 per student (Preply). One studio policy charges $30, or $70 for pieces that need an accompanist.
notes.recital_split: The recital fee is the total cost divided by the students performing, rounded up (teachbassoon.com).
notes.music_copies: Music at recitals: the Copyright Office's guidelines for educational uses of music don't allow copying music for a performance, except emergency copies when purchased copies can't arrive in time, replaced with purchased copies later (Circular 21).
notes.performance: A recital with no admission charge, no pay to the performers, promoters or organizers and no commercial purpose may fit the live performance exemption in 17 U.S.C. 110(4). One that promotes your studio or charges admission may not: ask the venue about its music performance licenses, and get legal advice when unsure.
notes.check: Background checks and home business rules vary: check your city and state.
